expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: Your not-empty test would have been green the entire time. It's not a weak device, it's a zero device — it has never had a chance to go red

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: The COALESCE(x, 0) is doing double duty here... It converted 'this join found nothing' into 'this customer earned nothing' — two facts that are indistinguishable downstream. That's the data equivalent of except: pass

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: Reconciliation to source. Warehouse revenue total vs. the billing system's total for the same window, asserted to a tolerance. If you install one thing, this.

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: Assert between load and publish. Build to staging → test staging → promote on pass. If your tests run after publication, bad numbers still reach the dashboard

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: A schema contract on the upstream table. A rename is a drop plus an add, and a drop should fail your ingest, not silently produce nulls.

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: Null-rate assertion on the join key, *before* the coalesce... assert null_rate < baseline on the pre-coalesce column. Volume/magnitude bounds on the metric itself

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Does not explicitly identify the three-week detection lag as a finding requiring its own solution. Recommends detection mechanisms but does not frame the lag itself as a problem to fix.

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: No comparison made between silent wrongness and failed pipeline. Does not explain why masking a loud failure into a plausible number is more dangerous than letting it fail.
